stack.engine: smoltcp 0.11.0 (std, medium-ip, proto-ipv4, proto-ipv6, socket-tcp, socket-udp)
stack.device: bounded Medium::Ip RX/TX queues (256 packets each), MTU from configuration
stack.registry: strong references; MAX_STACKS=64; idle (60 s, no socket) reaped by a 5 s sweep; explicit l3::forget / wireguard::forget_carrier (shutdown notify)
stack.tcp: smoltcp tcp::Socket behind AsyncRead/AsyncWrite; poll_shutdown sends FIN; remote FIN is EOF; RST is ConnectionReset; connect timeout is TimedOut; limit is OutOfMemory naming the maximum
stack.udp: unconnected smoltcp udp::Socket, many destinations per association, oversized datagram is InvalidInput naming the MTU

memory.formula: ~5.9 MiB + 0.125 MiB * peers per active stack; MAX_STACKS 64 => ~378 MiB + 8 MiB * peers

stack.tcp_admission: 16 concurrent sockets; excess dials wait for a slot (max 64 waiters, dial timeout), then connect; smoltcp timeout 60 s + keepalive 30 s

wireguard.peer_selection: longest matching allowed-ips prefix; equal lengths: later peer wins; missing prefix is a named no-route failure
wireguard.carrier: per-peer lazy actor; connect_carrier only resolves/binds; first packet or dial ensure_peer handshakes; per-peer failure drops only that peer; egress LPM; dispatcher 500 Hz
verified: IPv4 ICMP/UDP/TCP echo through the locked wireguard-go device
one live peer plus one dead endpoint: live dial/UDP succeed, dead dial fails by name, no fallback
two live peers selected by allowed-ips
IPv4/IPv6 stack behaviour and MTU bounds against the independent in-tree peer
not_verified: IPv6 through the Go wireguard-go peer (fixture answers IPv4 only)

openvpn.carrier: one dedicated OS thread; lazy stack handoff outside registry lock; send_id starts at 1; ping/ping-restart timers; TCP length-prefix FrameBuffer; replay/out-of-window packets dropped
verified: control channel over UDP and TCP framing, TLS and key-method 2 against OpenVPN 2.7.9
PUSH_REPLY prefixes/routes/dns/dhcp-option DNS/redirect/block-ipv6/push-continuation/auth-token/ping parsing and multi-segment accumulation (unit tests)
AEAD keepalive decryption over UDP and TCP
real routable Docker peer (--dev tun0, 10.8.0.1/24): connect_stack local 10.8.0.2, TCP echo hello-ovpn, UDP echo udp-ovpn from 10.8.0.1:7778
container and cert directory removed by a Drop guard after success/failure
not_verified: OpenVPN UDP control transport against a real TUN (Docker Desktop UDP port mapping is unreliable on macOS); control UDP is covered against --dev null and payload UDP is covered inside the TCP-controlled tunnel

consumers.tcp: outbound::dial_inner Protocol::Wireguard / Protocol::OpenVpn return a real stream; no DIRECT fallback
consumers.udp_engine: engine.rs serve_udp_associate_inner has WireGuard (guard option.udp) and OpenVPN send/receive arms over one L3 UDP socket
consumers.udp_tunnel: tunnel/udp.rs Transport::L3 shared by WireGuard and OpenVPN; the association resolves domain targets through the existing IP-only helper

anti_loop.openvpn: udp_socket_std_blocking / tcp_stream_std_blocking for the control link

tests.default_suite: pass (222 lib tests plus every default integration suite, --test-threads=1)
tests.device_vpn_suite: pass, including l3_stack 12/12; desktop-tun also passes (256 lib)

openvpn_docker.skip_conditions: KC_OPENVPN_DOCKER unset, docker unavailable, openssl unavailable, /dev/net/tun unavailable

concerns: OpenVPN real payload is verified over TCP control against a routable Docker TUN peer; the UDP control transport with a real TUN is not separately tested because Docker Desktop UDP forwarding is unreliable. --dev null remains only a control-plane case, not a payload claim.
IPv6 through the WireGuard fixture is not verified (locked Go peer answers IPv4 only); IPv6 is covered by the independent in-memory L3 peer.
The option matrix was not regenerated (needs a release kernel and pinned Mihomo); ip-stack rows are unchanged and only the note text changed.
OpenVPN tran-window and handshake-timeout are accepted but not enforced; renegotiation is not implemented. auth-token is recognized but unused.
forget/forget_carrier/openvpn::forget are not wired into engine reload/close; idle reaping is the only automatic teardown path.
The strong registry caps active stacks at 64; a config activating more proxies at once is refused by name.

TCP admission waiters are wake-all and re-check; the queue is bounded at 64 but not strictly FIFO, so slot acquisition is not guaranteed in arrival order. The timeout error names 16 slots and the wait duration.

repair.P1-1: WireGuard peers are lazy: connect_carrier resolves/binds only; first packet or dial ensure_peer handshakes; per-peer failure drops only that peer; dial selects by allowed-ips, ensures that peer, never falls back; Dialed.server is the resolved endpoint. Registry lock now covers only double-check lookup/publish; OVPN thread handoff is outside it.
repair.P1-2: TCP admission waits for a slot (MAX_TCP_WAITERS 64) within the dial timeout instead of failing at 16; sockets set smoltcp timeout 60 s and keepalive 30 s; tests cover wait-then-success, bounded queue, and timeout reclaim.
repair.P1-3: OpenVPN run_datapath takes ping/ping-restart (pushed values preferred) and tracks last_inbound/last_sent: ping sends keepalives, ping-restart fails on inbound silence.
repair.P3-4: PushReply parses dhcp-option DNS, block-ipv6, push-continuation, auth-token (recognized, not used) and ping/ping-restart with unit coverage.
repair.P3-5: Replayed/out-of-window data packet ids return Replay and recv_data drops them (continue); named LINK_READ_TIMEOUT=50 ms matches the blocking link read.
repair.P3-6: Registries hold strong references: l3 MAX_STACKS=64, WireGuard carrier registry strong with shutdown notify, 5 s idle sweep, explicit l3::forget/wireguard::forget/openvpn::forget; idle reap unit test. Stack poller is 500 Hz.
repair.P3-7: Per-stack memory table and formula documented: 1 MiB TCP + 4 MiB UDP + 2x256xmtu device + 128 KiB/peer scratch; MAX_STACKS 64 => ~378 MiB + 8 MiB*peers.
repair.P3-8: OVPN TCP framing uses FrameBuffer so a read timeout keeps partial frames; unit test plus a real OpenVPN 2.7.9 tcp4-server round trip. The TCP run also proved packet-id must start at 1.
repair.A3-P1: Routable Docker OpenVPN peer + default-skipped test; real TCP/UDP payload echo verified, container cleanup guard.
repair.A3-P3: forget hooks documented as API-only (not engine-wired); poller stop check under one lock with recheck and second ensure after socket creation; WG keepalive touches; TCP admission timeout names 16 slots and wait duration; WG UDP outside allowed-ips returns named NoRoute; multi-segment PUSH_REPLY accumulated; stale evidence contradictions removed.
